questions.q: Fresh PX4 1.18 firmware on a Pixhawk 6X, default parameters. `gimbal status` answers "not running". Why?
options: The `gimbal` module is not in the default fmu-v6x build
`MNT_MODE_IN` = −1, so `rcS` does not start the module
Output functions 420…422 are not assigned
`MNT_MODE_OUT` = 0 requires a connected gimbal
questions.explain: `rcS` has the condition `if param greater -s MNT_MODE_IN -1`; the default is −1, so the module does not start. The fmu-v6x `default.px4board` does have `CONFIG_MODULES_GIMBAL=y`, and output functions or a connected gimbal do not affect startup.

questions.q: PX4 1.18, AUX output: `MNT_MIN_PITCH` = −60, `MNT_MAX_PITCH` = 60, `MIN` = 1100, `CENT` = 1460, `MAX` = 1900 µs, `MNT_DO_STAB` = 1, frame level, vehicle in flight. Pitch setpoint −75°. What is on the output?
questions.explain: First the angle is clamped by `MNT_MIN_PITCH`: θ = −60°. Lower half-axis: c = −60/60 = −1, pulse = `CENT` + c · (`CENT` − `MIN`) = 1100 µs. 1010 comes out without the clamp (c = −1.25), 1000 if you use a single line 1100…1900 without the clamp, and 1190 is the pulse for −45°.

questions.q: A servo gimbal on an AUX output with default `MNT_*` parameters (PX4 1.18) will not tilt the camera below −45°, although the mechanics allow −90°. What do you change?
options: `PWM_AUX_CENTn` 250 µs lower
`MNT_LND_P_MIN` = −90
`MNT_MIN_PITCH` = −90
`MNT_RC_IN_MODE` = 0 (angle)
questions.explain: The setpoint is clamped to `MNT_MIN_PITCH` / `MNT_MAX_PITCH`, −45 and +45 by default. A lower limit of −90 opens up nadir, the upper one stays. Moving `CENT` changes only the zero, not the command range; `MNT_LND_P_MIN` is already −90 and acts only on the ground; the stick mode does not change the limit. Before 1.18 the same was done with `MNT_RANGE_PITCH` = 180.

questions.q: PX4 1.18: `MNT_RC_IN_MODE` = 1, `MNT_RATE_PITCH` = 30 °/s, `MNT_MIN_PITCH` = −60, `MNT_MAX_PITCH` = 60, `MNT_TAU` = 0. The gimbal is at 0°, and the stick is held at −1.0 for four seconds. What angle do you get?
questions.explain: The rate is −30 °/s; over 4 s the integral would give −120°, but the angle is clamped at `MNT_MIN_PITCH` = −60° and hits the limit after only 2 s. `MNT_TAU` = 0 matters here: with the 0.3 default the filter sits inside the accumulation loop, and in 4 s the gimbal would turn only a few degrees.

questions.q: A companion sends `MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_PITCHYAW` to a PX4 1.18 autopilot (`MNT_MODE_IN` = 4) and gets `DENIED`. The most likely cause?
options: The command is not supported; you need `GIMBAL_MANAGER_SET_PITCHYAW`
The sender has no primary control: `DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE` first
The angles are outside `MNT_MIN_PITCH` / `MNT_MAX_PITCH`
The companion port is not in `MAV_n_MODE` = 10
questions.explain: `input_mavlink.cpp` compares the sender's sysid and compid with the primary control owner and answers `DENIED` on a mismatch. There is no `GIMBAL_MANAGER_SET_PITCHYAW` handler at all in 1.17.0 and 1.18.0; the range does not affect the answer; the Gimbal set (10) is for the gimbal's own port, not the companion's.

questions.q: A MAVLink gimbal acting as a Gimbal v2 device is connected, `MNT_MODE_OUT` = 2. Which PX4 parameters still limit its angles?
options: `MNT_MIN_PITCH` / `MNT_MAX_PITCH` and `MNT_TAU`
Only `MNT_LND_P_MIN` / `MNT_LND_P_MAX`, and only on the ground
`MNT_DO_STAB` and `MNT_RANGE_*`
None: the quaternion goes to the device as is
questions.explain: For the v2 output the angle calculation function is not called: `GIMBAL_DEVICE_SET_ATTITUDE` carries the setpoint and lock flags with no limits, filter or stabilization. The gimbal handles the limits itself. `MNT_MIN_PITCH` / `MNT_MAX_PITCH`, `MNT_RANGE_*`, `MNT_TAU`, `MNT_LND_P_*`, `MNT_DO_STAB` work for AUX.

questions.q: Pixhawk 6X, PX4 1.18, capture in a Survey mission. What is wrong in this fragment?
questions.fragment:
TRIG_MODE         4
TRIG_INTERFACE    4
TRIG_DISTANCE     18
TRIG_MIN_INTERVA  1200
TRIG_ACT_TIME     40
PWM_MAIN_FUNC5    2000
PWM_AUX_TIM1      50
options: `TRIG_MODE` = 4 does not work with a mission; you need 1
`TRIG_ACT_TIME` = 40 ms is too short for PWM
Function 2000 is on an IO output: the driver looks for it in `PWM_AUX_FUNCn`
`TRIG_INTERFACE` = 4 requires `TRIG_POLARITY` = 1
questions.explain: On a board with an IO processor the `camera_trigger` driver is built with the `PWM_AUX` prefix and reads only `PWM_AUX_FUNCn`; the trigger works only on FMU outputs. Mode 4 is exactly the one for Survey, 40 ms is the minimum allowed time for PWM, and `TRIG_POLARITY` applies only to GPIO.

questions.q: `TRIG_DISTANCE` = 18 m, groundspeed 12 m/s, `TRIG_MIN_INTERVA` = 2000 ms, frame along the track 90 m. What forward overlap do you actually get?
questions.explain: The 18/12 = 1.5 s interval is shorter than 2 s: the driver skips (does not delay) every other release, having already moved the distance reference point. The spacing becomes 36 m, overlap 1 − 36/90 = 60 %.

questions.q: No hot shoe feedback. Speed 12 m/s, the camera fires 250 ms after the command. Where does the frame position from `camera_capture` lie relative to the true capture point?
options: 3 m behind along the flight direction
3 m ahead along the flight direction
0.3 m behind along the flight direction
It matches: PX4 interpolates the position
questions.explain: Without feedback `camera_feedback` records the time and position of the command. The shutter fires 0.25 s later, and in that time the vehicle moves 12 · 0.25 = 3 m forward, so the recorded point stays behind. `camera_feedback` does no interpolation to the frame time.

questions.q: `CAM_CAP_FBACK` = 1, function 2032 is assigned, but the wire from the hot shoe broke. What ends up in the log after the survey?
options: `camera_capture` with command positions, as without feedback
`camera_capture` is empty; the commands remain in `camera_trigger`
Both topics are empty
`camera_capture` with `result` = 0 for every frame
questions.explain: With feedback enabled `camera_feedback` discards `camera_trigger` records with `feedback = false` and builds `camera_capture` only from hot shoe signals. No signals, so the topic is empty. The release commands are still published to `camera_trigger`, and geotags can be rebuilt from them and `vehicle_global_position`.
